notes: Column/card ids are TEXT and reuse the same string ids the frontend already generates (createId() in kanban.ts, e.g. 'col-backlog', 'card-1'), so the API can return BoardData with no id-translation layer.
Exactly one board per user is enforced by the UNIQUE constraint on boards.user_id, not by application logic.
position columns hold each row's index within its parent (column position within a board, card position within a column) and reconstruct the ordering of BoardData.columns / Column.cardIds.
No indexes beyond primary/unique keys: MVP data volume is one user with one small board, so a table scan is fine.
ON DELETE CASCADE throughout: deleting a user/board/column cleans up its children, since no code path relies on orphaned rows.

tables.name: users
tables.description: One row per user. The MVP only ever creates the single hardcoded 'user' row, but the schema does not assume that.

tables.name: boards
columns
tables.description: The Kanban columns belonging to a board, in display order. Maps to BoardData.columns.

tables.name: cards
tables.description: The cards belonging to a column, in display order. Maps to BoardData.cards plus each Column.cardIds ordering.
tables.create_table_sql:
CREATE TABLE cards (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    column_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    details TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    position INTEGER NOT NULL
);

relationships.note: UNIQUE on boards.user_id enforces one board per user
